title: The trombonist and bass trumpeter who left for New York
summary: Handy praises a trombonist, probably Johnny Mandel, who left to join the bebop movement.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: He was a trombone player as I recall.
Yes, and he eventually moved over to the bass trumpet, he played bass trumpet for a while.
He played trombone on Boyd's band, but I think when he played with Basie I have an idea that he may have been playing bass trumpet.
Woody had bass trumpet, I didn't know Basie had bass trumpet.
I think when John was with him he hight have been playing it. I'm not positive. I just recall that that was the period he was playing bass trumpet and I assumed that's what he would do with Basie.
I don't remember ever hearing him.
One of the most musical jazz soloists you would have heard; just a marvelous musician all around. It was painful when he left the band. I felt a hole ripped in the band.
Why did he leave the band, where did he go?

He wanted to go back to New York because something was stirring in New York that had been started by Diz and Bird, that whole musical movement was happening at that point and he wanted to get more involved with it; he wanted to go back to New York.
